title: Microsoft Purview: network DLP for server and VM traffic through Azure Firewall
summary: Hold: the enforcement checklist omits activating the Purview policy after starting it in simulation. Microsoft requires an active policy and an On rule as well as the two blocking settings; following the checklist as written can leave protection unenforced.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans network-layer Purview DLP through Azure Firewall for sensitive text, files and AI interactions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview extends data security controls to the network layer through integration with Azure Firewall, helping organizations detect and protect sensitive data in supported network traffic, including text, files, and AI interactions.

claims.claim: The planned enforcement covers traffic from servers, virtual machines and other endpoints, including background services and automated workloads.
claims.quote: Organizations are able to enforce DLP policies on traffic from servers, virtual machines, and other endpoints, including traffic generated by background services and automated workloads.

claims.claim: The roadmap names sharing with cloud applications through browsers, applications and APIs.
claims.quote: These controls help prevent unauthorized sharing with cloud applications through browsers, applications, and APIs.

claims.claim: The DLP profile Mode options are Disabled, Alert only, and Alert and deny.
claims.quote: For Mode, select Alert only. This mode monitors without blocking, including when Microsoft Purview returns a deny decision. The other options are Disabled and Alert and deny.

claims.claim: Alert only does not block even if Purview returns a deny decision.
claims.quote: This mode monitors without blocking, including when Microsoft Purview returns a deny decision.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, enforcement bullet
claims.claim: After starting the policy in simulation, the checklist moves to enforcement by setting Block and Alert and deny without requiring policy activation or an On rule.
claims.quote: Configure the relevant Purview rule action as Block, keep the rule On, and activate the policy rather than leaving it in simulation or audit.
claims.fix: Replace the enforcement bullet with: 'Move to enforcement only after review: set the Purview rule action to Block, keep the rule On, activate the policy rather than leaving it in simulation or audit, and set the firewall profile Mode to Alert and deny, then repeat the tests.'

claims.quote: Searched: 'New-DlpCompliancePolicy New-DlpComplianceRule Network non-Microsoft secure browsers Inline web traffic PowerShell Locations'; opened both cmdlet references. Network is an EnforcementPlanes value, but no complete network-location/action call is documented.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Azure Firewall AI Security DLP security profile group application rule REST API PowerShell CLI Terraform'; opened ai-security-concepts and configure-network-dlp. AI Security protections are portal-only; general firewall rule automation does not document this group attachment.

claims.where: Open questions: background services and automated workloads

claims.claim: Every control the checklist tells readers to configure or check has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Check that TLS inspection works'; 'give that identity Storage Blob Data Contributor'; 'Review DLP Alerts and Activity explorer'. Table: only the Purview policy, firewall DLP profile Mode and application-rule group selection.
claims.fix: The Before rollout TLS-inspection check and mapping-file identity-role assignment, and the After rollout DLP Alerts/Activity explorer review, have no matching controls-table rows. Remove those checklist steps; their factual context can remain in the body. Do not add control rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Learn's evaluation procedure tests synthetic protected content and a benign control.
claims.quote: Transfer synthetic protected content and a benign control through the same source, destination, and activity.

claims.quote: Searched: '"New-DlpCompliancePolicy" "Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers" automation'; opened and searched the full reference for Network, browser, Inline, Locations and EnforcementPlanes. It lists a Network plane value, but no dedicated location parameter or example.
